personas.summary: A strong, unusually well-verified amines chapter. I checked all 26 asset SMILES and every SMILES in the 56 questions with RDKit against formula, canonical connectivity and InChIKey, and every one is the compound it claims to be, including the stereo-defined azo dye, the 2,4-dinitroaniline pattern, histamine's C4 attachment and quinoline versus isoquinoline. I independently re-derived every answer key and all 56 are correct. Roughly twenty quoted pKa values check out against literature and are internally consistent. Of the three late-added passages, two are sound; the third introduced a quantitative claim its own numbers refute. My verdict is NOT-GO as written on one narrow but hard defect: the accessible descriptions of both Hofmann drawing questions call primary amines secondary, which is precisely the misconception concept 1 exists to prevent. Beyond it, no amine nomenclature is taught although several items require name-to-structure translation, and the halogen substituent case is graded twice while the rule the chapter states predicts the wrong sign for it.

location.anchor_text: exhaustive methylation of a five-carbon secondary amine

findings.observation: Both Hofmann drawing questions misclassify their starting amine in the accessible_description, calling 2-aminopentane and 3-methylbutan-2-amine secondary amines. Both are primary: in each the nitrogen carries exactly one carbon substituent. The descriptions classified the carbon rather than the nitrogen.
findings.learner_impact: Every learner who reads the description is taught the exact misconception the chapter's first concept is built to destroy, by the chapter itself. It also silently contradicts ch24-hofmann-equivalents, whose key of 3 equiv is correct only because sec-butylamine is primary; a student accepting secondary would compute 2 and be marked wrong with no way to reconcile the two items.
findings.evidence: Both accessible_descriptions say secondary amine; contradicted by nugget-amine-structure-classification practice_check, which states of the formula-identical case that sec-butylamine is a primary amine because classification counts carbon substituents on nitrogen.
findings.recommended_outcome: The two Hofmann drawing items need starting-material descriptions that classify the amine at nitrogen, and the chapter needs assurance no other item description classifies an amine by its carbon.

findings.observation: The chapter teaches no amine nomenclature at all, yet multiple graded items require translating an amine name into a structure with no structure supplied: 2-Aminopentane on a blank canvas, sec-Butylamine, N-Methylpiperidine, and parsing N,N-dimethylpentanamide versus N,N-dimethylpentan-1-amine. Three incompatible naming conventions are used across the chapter and none is introduced.
findings.learner_impact: Name-to-structure translation becomes an ungraded prerequisite silently gating graded chemistry; a student who understands Hofmann regiochemistry can fail by drawing the wrong skeleton, and the feedback about beta hydrogens will not diagnose it.
findings.evidence: No nugget text in any tier contains a naming rule and no concept covers nomenclature. ch24-hofmann-major-alkene-v2 supplies a condensed formula while its v1 twin supplies only the name.
findings.recommended_outcome: Either the chapter needs explicit amine-naming instruction in the default tier, or the name-only items need structures supplied so nomenclature is not an unstated gate.

location.anchor_text: One ring in the path, one discount; no ring in the path, no discount; two rings, twice the discount.

findings.observation: The closing line of the late-added benzylamine/diphenylamine paragraph asserts two rings deliver twice the discount of one. The chapter's own numbers refute it: aniline's discount is 10.7 minus 4.6 equals 6.1 units, so twice would put diphenylamine near minus 1.5, but diphenylamine is 0.8 and the paragraph says so two sentences earlier. The real second-ring increment is 3.8 units; the effects are strongly sublinear, partly because the two rings cannot both be coplanar with nitrogen.
findings.learner_impact: Hands students a false additive model that is memorable because it is tidy, produces wrong estimates for triphenylamine and any di-arylated nitrogen, and teaches that resonance effects simply add. An attentive student can see the sentence contradict the number beside it.
findings.evidence: nugget-arylamine-basicity expanded tier closing line; ch24-rank-aniline-substituents-v2 uses the same four values as its reference ladder.
findings.recommended_outcome: The summary line needs to match the data it just presented, showing the second ring adding a further smaller discount rather than doubling the first, ideally with a reason the increments are not additive.

location.anchor_text: The same electronic vocabulary that predicts electrophilic aromatic substitution rates thus predicts arylamine basicity, with no new ideas needed.

findings.observation: Halogen substituents are graded twice but never taught, and the stated rule predicts the wrong answer for them. The expanded tier discusses only nitro and methoxy and then tells students to reuse their EAS directing-effect vocabulary, which classifies chlorine as an ortho/para director, the same box as methoxy. Two items require the opposite. The reconciling idea, that halogens are inductively withdrawing but resonance-donating and induction wins for basicity, appears in no tier, only in a level-3 hint.
findings.learner_impact: A student reasoning exactly as instructed gets both items wrong, and the feedback states the conclusion without giving the mechanism. This is the one place where following the taught rule produces a wrong graded answer, which discredits a rule needed elsewhere.
findings.evidence: The expanded tier covers only p-nitro and p-methoxy; no tier mentions halogen, chlorine, or inductive-versus-resonance competition. Graded in ch24-strongest-arylamine option c and ch24-rank-aniline-substituents key order, and in the nugget's own practice_check.
findings.recommended_outcome: The default-tier prose needs to cover the halogen case explicitly so the substituent rule the chapter states actually covers every substituent it grades.

location.anchor_text: historically the chief industrial phenol synthesis

findings.observation: Warm hydrolysis of a diazonium salt is described as historically the chief industrial phenol synthesis. It never was: industrial phenol ran on benzenesulfonate/alkali fusion, then chlorobenzene hydrolysis, and since the 1950s overwhelmingly on the cumene hydroperoxide process. Diazonium hydrolysis consumes stoichiometric nitrite, needs ice-bath control and runs dilute. The rest of the sentence, about positional control, is correct.
findings.learner_impact: Students carry away a false piece of process chemistry contradicted in any industrial context, and it distorts why the diazonium route is valuable: positional control, not throughput.
findings.evidence: nugget-arenediazonium-chemistry expanded tier; note ch24-diazonium-route offers NaOH at 300 C as a distractor, so the actual historical industrial chemistry appears only as a wrong answer.
findings.recommended_outcome: The industrial attribution needs removing or correcting; the positional-control justification is accurate and sufficient alone.

location.anchor_text: eliminations with quaternary ammonium leaving groups give the less substituted alkene — is called the Hofmann rule

findings.observation: The Hofmann rule is stated without exception, as a property of the leaving group. The well-known exception, a beta hydrogen made acidic by an adjacent aryl or carbonyl group where the elimination acquires E1cb character and gives the conjugated more substituted alkene, is not mentioned anywhere.
findings.learner_impact: Students meeting a benzylic or carbonyl-activated substrate apply the steric rule confidently and get the wrong alkene, with no cue that a different control operates. It also implies regiochemistry is decided by leaving-group size alone.
findings.evidence: nugget-hofmann-elimination expanded tier; no tier contains acidic, conjugat-, E1cb or styrene. All four Hofmann assessment items use purely alkyl substrates.
findings.recommended_outcome: The section needs a bounding sentence stating the condition under which Hofmann orientation fails, so the rule carries its domain of validity.

location.anchor_text: Exhaustive methylation exploits precisely the runaway alkylation that plagued amine synthesis

findings.observation: Declared prerequisites do not match what the prose assumes, in both directions. hofmann-elimination declares only amine-structure-classification yet builds its central move on the overalkylation runaway from amine-synthesis-alkylation and its regiochemistry on E2/Zaitsev. Conversely reductive-amination declares amine-synthesis-alkylation but uses nothing from it. pyrrole-imidazole and pyridine-chemistry both lean on the protonation-destroys-stabilization argument from arylamine-basicity, which neither declares.
findings.learner_impact: The prerequisite graph drives adaptive sequencing and remediation; where it is wrong a stuck student is routed to the wrong concept.
findings.evidence: concepts[] prerequisite lists versus the dependency sentences in nugget-hofmann-elimination expanded.
findings.recommended_outcome: Prerequisite declarations need reconciling with the dependencies the prose actually asserts.

location.anchor_text: Use the azide synthesis and the Gabriel synthesis to prepare a primary amine cleanly.

findings.observation: The stated objective is to use the azide and Gabriel syntheses to make a primary amine, but every item on this concept is a failure case: why direct alkylation fails, how Gabriel avoids overalkylation, Gabriel failing on an aryl halide, azide failing on a tertiary halide. No item asks a student to execute a successful sequence, and neither synthesis_route item uses them. It is also the thinnest concept in the bank with 2 unique items.
findings.learner_impact: Students can pass every item while knowing only where the methods break, never having produced a primary amine by either route.
findings.evidence: The objective text versus the concept's four items; ch24-nitrile-route offers NaN3 only as a distractor.
findings.recommended_outcome: This concept needs at least one item in which a masked-nitrogen route succeeds and the student builds or draws the product.

location.anchor_text: LiAlH4 delivers two hydride equivalents to the C#N triple bond

findings.observation: Reader prose ships raw ASCII and SMILES-derived notation while question surfaces use correct typography. The compiled reader contains C#N triple bond, Ar-N#N+, LiAlH4 seventeen times, NaBH3CN, CH3I, N3-, 10^6 and 10^11; the questions render the same species with proper Unicode. The hash character is SMILES syntax, not chemical notation, and nothing tells the reader it means a triple bond.
findings.learner_impact: A student meeting C#N in prose and the Unicode triple bond in the next question must infer they are the same object, and unsubscripted formulas model habits that lose marks on handwritten work.
findings.evidence: grep counts against the compiled reader as listed; contrast ch24-choose-reducing-agent prompt.
findings.recommended_outcome: Prose and assessment need one shared notation convention, with the SMILES hash removed from student-facing text.

findings.observation: All 26 assets are static single-molecule depictions; the chapter contains no figure of a process, comparison or energy relationship. The places where the prose is explicitly describing a picture are exactly the places with no picture: the pKaH ladder, aniline's delocalization, the Hofmann E2 profile, the pyrrole-versus-pyridine lone-pair geometry, and the Hofmann rearrangement migration. The five video briefs that would carry this load compile hidden with empty urls.
findings.learner_impact: The chapter's hardest ideas are all spatial and all carried by prose alone; students get static structures for the easy content and nothing for the difficult content.
findings.evidence: All 26 assets are type molecule; every video block has an empty url and is_hidden true.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs process-level visual support where the reasoning is spatial, and the five briefs need either delivery or removal so the reader is not carrying dead blocks.

location.anchor_text: The conjugate acid of pyridine has pKa 5.2 and the conjugate acid of piperidine has pKa 11.1.

findings.observation: All ten nuggets carry a well-written practice_check with a worked answer and none reaches the reader; the compiled chapter contains zero occurrences and no block type that could render one. Several checks are the only place a skill is exercised at all.
findings.learner_impact: A student reading end to end encounters ten sections of continuous exposition with no point at which they must produce anything; the first retrieval attempt happens in the graded bank.
findings.evidence: grep -c practice_check on the compiled reader returns 0; all ten nuggets carry a populated object.
findings.recommended_outcome: The authored practice checks need to reach the reader, or the chapter needs to stop authoring content that is never delivered so the gap is visible in production rather than review.

location.anchor_text: Three reducing systems appear on exams

findings.observation: The nitro-reduction paragraph announces three reducing systems and lists two: catalytic hydrogenation over Pt or Pd, and Fe/Sn/SnCl2 in aqueous HCl. The terse tier lists the same two, so the third is not hiding in another tier.
findings.learner_impact: A student revising from this paragraph hunts for a missing third system and ends up with an off-by-one checklist.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction expanded tier.
findings.recommended_outcome: The count and the list need to agree.

location.anchor_text: roughly a hundred-million-fold weaker as a base than pyridine

findings.observation: The prose and question feedback disagree by an order of magnitude and the prose is wrong. The chapter's values give 5.2 minus minus 4 equals 9.2 log units, about a billion-fold; the prose says hundred-million-fold. The wrong-answer explanation states it correctly as some nine orders of magnitude.
findings.learner_impact: Small, but this chapter's pedagogy is explicitly built on converting pKa differences into factors, so a worked conversion off by ten undercuts the skill taught two sections earlier.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyrrole-imidazole expanded versus ch24-protonated-on-nitrogen-v2 option d explanation.
findings.recommended_outcome: The prose conversion needs to match the chapter's own pKaH values and the question feedback.

location.anchor_text: Neutral NH2- is among the worst leaving groups in chemistry

findings.observation: The standard tier opens by calling an anion neutral. The expanded tier states the same point correctly, so this is a tier-local slip. Relatedly, SnCl2 is grouped under dissolving-metal conditions although tin(II) chloride is a metal-salt reductant rather than a dissolving-metal system.
findings.learner_impact: Charge bookkeeping is the exact skill this chapter drills, so a leading sentence labelling a charged species neutral is a bad model at the worst moment.
findings.evidence: nugget-hofmann-elimination standard tier opening sentence; nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction expanded dissolving-metal grouping.
findings.recommended_outcome: The standard tier needs its leaving-group sentence corrected, and the dissolving-metal label scoped to the metals.

location.anchor_text: Read in McMurry (OpenStax) — Chapter 24

findings.observation: The compiled reader carries one mcmurry_link block, on section 1, pointing at the chapter front matter. Nine of ten sections have no textbook reading block. The Wikipedia links are per-section and well chosen; I checked all ten and each resolves to the correct article, so this is specifically an OpenStax-mapping gap in the reader blocks.
findings.learner_impact: Students wanting the textbook treatment of a specific section are dropped on the chapter opening page, and instructors cannot point at assigned readings section by section.
findings.evidence: Exactly one mcmurry_link block in the compiled reader, url ending 24-why-this-chapter.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs section-specific OpenStax targets in the reader blocks, matching the per-section granularity the Wikipedia links achieve.

location.anchor_text: Pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6) enzymes convert ketoacids to amino acids through iminium intermediates reduced or transaminated in the active site

findings.observation: The biology paragraph blurs two distinct reactions. PLP-dependent transamination is not a reductive amination: no hydride is delivered and no net reduction occurs; the amine arrives by a 1,3-proton shift and ketimine hydrolysis. The hedge reduced or transaminated lets the conflation stand. The glutamate dehydrogenase example in the same sentence is a genuine reductive amination and carries the point alone.
findings.learner_impact: Students going on to biochemistry meet transamination as mechanistically distinct and must unlearn the pairing.
findings.evidence: nugget-reductive-amination expanded final paragraph.
findings.recommended_outcome: The metabolic analogy needs to rest on the genuine reductive amination and either drop the PLP clause or mark transamination as related but different.

strengths: Every SMILES in the package is correct. All 26 assets and all 84 question structures verified with RDKit against formula, canonical connectivity and InChIKey, including cases where a formula-identical isomer was available to go wrong: the azo dye is correctly E-configured, 2,4-dinitroaniline has its nitro groups at 2 and 4, histamine is attached at imidazole C4, and quinoline is the 2,3-benzo-fused isomer.

Every answer key is chemically correct on independent re-derivation, including both anti-Zaitsev Hofmann products, both reductive-amination amine classes, the plus-one and minus-one carbon counts, the Chichibabin at C2, pyrrole at C2 and indole at C3, and every diazonium reagent-product pairing including the copper-free KI and the Schiemann route.
The pKa data are accurate and internally consistent across roughly twenty values checked against literature, used consistently in prose, options, hints and feedback.
The look-at-what-protonation-destroys framing converts memorized pKaH values into one transferable decision rule, and the structured_reasoning items grade the reasoning rather than the number.
The structured_reasoning items are unusually well built, each pairing a correct claim against a plausible competing claim and forcing rejection of an irrelevant physical property as evidence.

The two error_repair items are the best-designed assessment in the chapter: both put the flaw in the substrate rather than the reagent, offer a correct-but-not-flawed decoy claim, and include repairs that adjust conditions where no change of conditions can rescue a geometrically impossible step.
Coverage and type variety are strong: 56 items across 15 question types and all ten concepts, with a sensible difficulty spread and a v2 variant for every item, giving a usable retest form.
open_questions: I graded the industrial-phenol claim as medium rather than blocker because it is a false historical attribution rather than wrong reaction chemistry and no student will predict a wrong product from it. The orchestrator may wish to override.

The practice_check non-delivery and the hidden empty-url video blocks look like platform delivery gaps rather than authoring defects, and the same pattern has been reported for earlier chapters. Should these be filed against the chapter or tracked as a platform ticket?

ch24-hofmann-e2-ledger labels atom 2 as the terminal CH3 carbon bonded to atom 1. That is unambiguous on close reading but sec-butyl has a second terminal methyl, and a hurried student may pick it. I did not raise it as a finding.
Every item has demo_eligible false, so nothing can appear in a public sampler. Intentional or oversight?
The chapter states Hofmann orientation is steric, the standard textbook line. If the course wants the modern E1cb-character account that is a scope decision; I flagged only the missing exception.

personas.summary: As a student who is not fluent yet, I found this chapter unusually well-written at the sentence level and unusually hard to study from. The default (expanded) prose is careful about the things that normally trip me. What defeats me is structure and support, not content: no retrieval practice reaches the reader, the two list-shaped topics (pKaH ladder, diazonium menu) arrive as paragraphs, the three resonance arguments are asserted without any intermediate drawn, all five videos compile with an empty url, and the two different Hofmann reactions are never disambiguated.

location.anchor_text: The conjugate acid of pyridine has pKa 5.2 and the conjugate acid of piperidine has pKa 11.1.

findings.observation: All ten nuggets carry a practice_check and none reaches the compiled reader; sections contain only text, molecule, video, mcmurry_link and external_link blocks.
findings.learner_impact: A low-confidence student reads 3,000-4,000 characters per section with no way to test retention, then meets a graded question cold.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json nuggets each have practice_check; compiled reader has 53 blocks across 10 sections, none a practice block.
findings.recommended_outcome: The student needs a low-stakes retrieval checkpoint per section; the authored self-check content exists but never reaches the learner surface.

location.anchor_text: methylamine 10.6, ethylamine 10.8, dimethylamine 10.7, cyclohexylamine 10.7, and the cyclic secondary amine piperidine at 11.1

findings.observation: Section 2 delivers roughly fourteen pKaH values entirely in running prose with no ladder, table or ordered visual anywhere in the chapter.
findings.learner_impact: Six ranking/selection questions ask the student to order these compounds; holding fourteen numbers from four paragraphs in working memory forces guessing.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-basicity expanded paragraphs 2-3; section assets are only mol-cyclohexylamine and mol-acetamide.
findings.recommended_outcome: The basicity ladder is the chapter's central organizing structure and needs a form a student can see at once and return to.

location.anchor_text: Attack at C2 delocalizes the cation over C3, C5

findings.observation: The three regiochemistry arguments (pyrrole C2, pyridine C3, indole C3) are all settled by counting resonance structures of a cationic intermediate, and none is ever drawn. The pyridine sentence contains a literal unfinished enumeration: 'Attack at C2 delocalizes the cation over C3, C5... and the nitrogen'.
findings.learner_impact: Question hints instruct the student to draw the cationic intermediate and write out resonance forms, a procedure the chapter never demonstrates; students fall back on pattern-matching that fails on the indole item.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyridine-chemistry paragraph 2 and nugget-pyrrole-imidazole paragraph 3; ch24-pyridine-eas-position, -v2, ch24-fused-heterocycle-reactivity-v2 turn on these counts.
findings.recommended_outcome: A student needs one sigma-complex argument worked through with competing intermediates and charge locations, and the truncated enumeration must be completed.

location.anchor_text: The Hofmann rearrangement subtracts a carbon, and its mechanism is more interesting than a simple reduction.

findings.observation: Two entirely different reactions share a name (Hofmann rearrangement in section 5, Hofmann elimination in section 7) and no sentence anywhere acknowledges the collision. Section 7 adds 'the Hofmann rule' as a third use.
findings.learner_impact: Installs a permanent wrong mental model; a student meeting 'a Hofmann rearrangement' in a question looks for iodomethane and silver oxide and concludes they misunderstood a section.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction paragraph 4 vs nugget-hofmann-elimination throughout; ch24-nitrile-carbon-count-v2 vs ch24-hofmann-* items sit in the same bank.
findings.recommended_outcome: The student needs an explicit disambiguation of the two Hofmann reactions: what each starts from, produces, and does to the carbon count.

location.anchor_text: the replacement menu, which should be learned as a table because exams treat it as one

findings.observation: The prose tells the student this content should be learned as a table and then delivers seven reagent-product pairs as a single 250-word paragraph with no table or figure.
findings.learner_impact: The chapter names the form the knowledge needs and refuses to supply it; students guess on the H3PO2 and warm-water pairs in both matching items.
findings.evidence: nugget-arenediazonium-chemistry paragraph 3; ch24-diazonium-reagent-match and -v2 test exactly this list.
findings.recommended_outcome: List-shaped knowledge tested as a list needs a scannable, rehearsable presentation rather than continuous prose.

location.anchor_text: Three reducing systems appear on exams:

findings.observation: The sentence announces three reducing systems for nitroarenes and then lists two (H2/Pt or Pd; Fe or Sn or SnCl2 in aqueous HCl).
findings.learner_impact: A student counting along searches backward for content that is not there and goes into an exam believing the list is incomplete.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction expanded paragraph 3.
findings.recommended_outcome: The promised count and the delivered list must agree.

location.anchor_text: which tautomerizes and dehydrates under the acidic conditions to the arenediazonium ion

findings.observation: Five load-bearing terms are used in the default expanded tier without gloss and without a named earlier chapter: tautomerizes, cumulated pi system, Huckel criterion (4n+2 never appears), anti-periplanar, anilides.
findings.learner_impact: Diazotization becomes a black box; 'the usual anti-periplanar geometry' signals the student should already know something they do not.
findings.evidence: nugget-arenediazonium-chemistry para 1; nugget-amine-synthesis-alkylation para 2; nugget-pyrrole-imidazole para 1; nugget-hofmann-elimination para 2; nugget-arylamine-basicity para 4.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each term needs its meaning attached at point of use or an explicit pointer to where it was established.

location.anchor_text: Pyrrole, whose nitrogen lone pair is built into its aromatic sextet, barely protonates at all

findings.observation: Section 2 explains pyrrole's and pyridine's ladder positions using 'aromatic sextet' and the in-plane-vs-pi lone pair distinction, but the sextet is not defined until section 9 and the pyridine geometry until section 10.
findings.learner_impact: Two of five cliffs are memorized as brute facts with reasons deferred seven sections, and the connection is never made when the explanation finally arrives.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-basicity paragraph 3 vs nugget-pyrrole-imidazole paragraph 1 and nugget-pyridine-chemistry paragraph 1.
findings.recommended_outcome: Either a one-line working definition where the idea is first used, or an explicit forward-reference marker.

location.anchor_text: para-methoxyaniline's oxygen feeds density into the ring

findings.observation: The five-card ranking needs p-methylaniline 5.1 and p-chloroaniline 4.0, but the default expanded prose supplies values only for aniline, p-nitroaniline and p-methoxyaniline. The two missing facts appear only in the practice_check answer, which never compiles.
findings.learner_impact: Two of five positions rest on facts a default reader has never seen, forcing import from the aromatic-substitution chapter.
findings.evidence: nugget-arylamine-basicity paragraph 3 mentions only nitro and methoxy; 5.1 and 4.0 appear only in the practice_check answer.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every comparison a ranking item scores should be derivable from what the default-tier reader actually shows.

location.anchor_text: even that number refers to protonation on C2, not nitrogen

findings.observation: Section 9 says pyrrole's pKaH of about -4 refers to protonation on C2, not nitrogen. The wrong-answer explanation on ch24-protonated-on-nitrogen attaches the same number to nitrogen protonation.
findings.learner_impact: A student who notices the careful caveat is contradicted by the feedback and stops attending to that level of precision.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyrrole-imidazole paragraph 2 vs feedback_bundle.wrong_answer_explanations option b of ch24-protonated-on-nitrogen; ch24-rank-basicity-v2 hint level 3 also uses -4 unqualified.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter and its question feedback need to agree about what the -4 value measures.

location.anchor_text: One arrow only: from the nitrogen's lone pair to the carbonyl carbon.

findings.observation: Level-3 hints on both curved-arrow items state the complete answer verbatim, naming the exact source and target sites the answer key expects.
findings.learner_impact: Students learn to open hint 3 first, losing the one skill the item exists to build.
findings.evidence: feedback_bundle.hints level 3 of ch24-reductive-amination-arrow and -v2 vs answer_key.expected_arrows.
findings.recommended_outcome: The final hint needs to leave one decision to the student rather than reading out the answer key.

location.anchor_text: Reductive amination step by step: carbonyl in, amine out

findings.observation: Five video blocks compile into the reader with an empty url, each showing a title and storyboard-style description. All five briefs are production_status deferred and cover exactly the electron-flow, orbital and multi-step content the 26 static figures cannot carry.
findings.learner_impact: The student clicks a playable-looking block, nothing plays, and reads a description of content that does not exist.
findings.evidence: compiled reader video blocks in six sections with empty url; topic.package.json video_briefs all deferred.
findings.recommended_outcome: Either the five explanations need some delivered form, or an unproduced brief should not surface as a playable-looking block.

location.anchor_text: But the pyramid is not frozen. It inverts through a planar, sp2-like transition state

findings.observation: The third paragraph of the chapter's first section introduces about ten new ideas in seven sentences, several prerequisite-heavy (hybridization, transition state, resolution of enantiomers).
findings.learner_impact: This is where a student calibrates whether they can keep up; ten ideas on page one triggers a switch from understanding to memorizing.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-structure-classification expanded paragraph 3; section assets are four static molecules plus an empty-url video.
findings.recommended_outcome: The inversion chain of reasoning needs breaking into steps with the consequence stated before the numbers.

location.anchor_text: giving after proton shuffling a carbinolamine

findings.observation: The full reductive-amination mechanism is delivered as one paragraph of continuous prose; the section's only figures are the starting ketone and finished amine, and neither intermediate the student is later asked about is drawn.
findings.learner_impact: Students retrieve words without a picture of the sequence, producing the exact oxygen-in-product error the generic feedback anticipates.
findings.evidence: nugget-reductive-amination expanded paragraph 1; asset_ids only mol-cyclohexanone and mol-n-methylcyclohexylamine.
findings.recommended_outcome: The carbonyl to carbinolamine to iminium to amine sequence needs to be visible as discrete stages before intermediates are named and arrows drawn.

location.anchor_text: Name the process, occurring roughly a hundred billion times per second, that is responsible.

findings.observation: The question asks students to name a process the default expanded tier never names; 'pyramidal inversion' and 'umbrella flip' appear only in the terse and standard tiers and the unproduced video title.
findings.learner_impact: Being asked to name something the chapter never named reads as having skipped a paragraph; a low-confidence student leaves it blank.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-structure-classification expanded paragraph 3 vs answer_key.answer_text of ch24-nitrogen-inversion; _detail_texts.terse and .standard are alternatives to the shown tier.
findings.recommended_outcome: A term a question asks a student to produce needs to appear in the tier the reader shows by default.

location.anchor_text: roughly a hundred-million-fold weaker as a base than pyridine

findings.observation: Pyrrole -4 and pyridine 5.2 differ by 9.2 units, a factor of about 10^9, but the prose says 'a hundred-million-fold' (10^8). The question feedback correctly says 'some nine orders of magnitude'.
findings.learner_impact: Section 2 trains the student to convert pKa gaps into factors; doing so here contradicts the text and destroys trust in their own arithmetic.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyrrole-imidazole paragraph 2 vs nugget-amine-basicity practice_check and ch24-protonated-on-nitrogen-v2 option d explanation.
findings.recommended_outcome: A quantitative claim the student is explicitly taught to check by subtraction has to survive that check.

location.anchor_text: the classical dissolving-metal conditions that tolerate no strong-acid-sensitive groups but leave alkenes and carbonyls alone better than catalytic hydrogenation does

findings.observation: The clause packs a negative-tolerance and a comparative-selectivity statement into one sentence, and 'tolerate no strong-acid-sensitive groups' inverts the usual sense of tolerate.
findings.learner_impact: The student cannot tell whether Fe/HCl is the safer or riskier choice, the only thing needed for two synthesis-route questions.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction expanded paragraph 3.
findings.recommended_outcome: The compatibility trade-off is decision-relevant for two route questions and needs stating in a form a student can act on.

location.anchor_text: p-Toluidine

personas.summary: The authoring side is among the strongest in this pipeline: all 26 assets carry alt_text and long_description, all 56 questions carry an accessible_description, find_accessibility_leaks returns zero hits, and the expanded prose is genuinely text-first. The two reaction_coordinate_reasoning items are clean, reporting curve geometry and relative heights without stating step count or the exergonic classification. The barriers are elsewhere. Two are hard: the four structure_scaffold items are answerable only by drawing on a Ketcher canvas whose toolbar profile hides paste, so there is no text path in; and ch24-hofmann-equivalents-v2's description classifies the amine as cyclic tertiary, which is exactly what determines the requested count. Beyond those, most authored accessibility payload never reaches a student, and two descriptions mislabel a primary amine as secondary.

location.anchor_text: A blank drawing canvas is provided.

findings.observation: All four structure_scaffold items set scaffold to blank_canvas and are graded against answer_key.smiles. StructureWorkspaceRenderer embeds the generator as an iframe with toolbarProfile lti_drawing, which hides open, save, copies, paste and cut, so a learner cannot even paste a SMILES as a substitute for pointer drawing. There is no SMILES field, no name entry, and no alternate activity.
findings.learner_impact: A learner who is blind, low-vision, screen-reader dependent, or keyboard/switch-navigating cannot submit any response to these four items, and therefore also cannot receive the feedback or hint ladder everyone else gets.
findings.evidence: ch24-reductive-amination-product, -v2, ch24-hofmann-major-alkene, -v2 each have student_config [redacted]; [internal source reference — not in this repo] renders only the iframe and a link to the same drawing surface.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every learner needs a way to express a drawn structure without a pointer on a canvas; the product identity is expressible in text, so the need is a non-drawing response path or an equivalent alternate item. No concept becomes unassessable, since both concepts carry other question types.

location.anchor_text: The question describes converting a named cyclic tertiary amine to its quaternary ammonium iodide with iodomethane.

findings.observation: The item asks how many equivalents of iodomethane are consumed taking N-methylpiperidine to its quaternary salt (answer 1). Equivalents equal four minus the carbons already on nitrogen, and the chapter states that rule directly. The accessible_description classifies the amine as cyclic tertiary, handing over the answer in one trivial step. The v1 twin says only 'a named amine'.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader learner is given the one fact the item tests, so their score is not comparable to a sighted peer's, reversing the equity the bundle exists to provide.
findings.evidence: ch24-hofmann-equivalents-v2 answer_key value 1 unit equiv; contrast ch24-hofmann-equivalents description which gives no classification.
findings.recommended_outcome: The description needs to convey the stimulus without performing the classification step the item grades, matching the neutral phrasing the v1 item already uses.

location.anchor_text: accessibility_bundle

findings.observation: All 56 items carry an authored accessible_description that survives compilation, but only ReactionCoordinateQuestionRenderer consumes it for the types this chapter uses. Thirteen other renderers contain no reference to accessibilityBundle, so 54 of 56 descriptions are inert metadata.
findings.learner_impact: Where item controls happen to carry good labels the learner is fine; where they do not, the learner gets no orienting description of the stimulus even though a good one was written and shipped.
findings.evidence: grep for accessibilityBundle across activity-renderers returns hits only in MolecularGeometryRenderer and ReactionCoordinateQuestionRenderer.
findings.recommended_outcome: The authored per-item stimulus description needs a delivery path all renderers honour. Platform-level gap recurring from ch16/ch21/ch22.

location.anchor_text: Pyridine: a six-membered aromatic ring in which one CH unit of benzene is replaced by a nitrogen.

findings.observation: Every asset carries a long_description doing the real chemical work, and none reaches the reader; the compiled chapter contains zero occurrences of long_description. For 12 of 26 assets the alt_text alone then omits the lone-pair or formal-charge fact the figure exists to teach. mol-pyrrole and mol-pyridine alt texts are nearly interchangeable on the one contrast that matters.
findings.learner_impact: A learner relying on alt text gets a shape inventory; for the pyrrole-versus-pyridine contrast the figures teach that learner nothing, though the surrounding prose does state it.
findings.evidence: mol-pyridine long_description explains the in-plane sp2 lone pair; the compiled block carries only name, smiles, alt_text, description, generator_href.

location.anchor_text: exhaustive methylation of a five-carbon secondary amine

findings.observation: Both hofmann-major-alkene descriptions misclassify their starting material. 2-Aminopentane and 3-methylbutan-2-amine each have a nitrogen bearing exactly one carbon, so both are primary amines; the descriptions call them secondary. The prompts do not use the word, so the error is introduced only in the accessibility channel.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader learner is fed a statement contradicting the chapter's core classification convention at the moment they must apply bookkeeping that depends on that count; sighted learners never see it.
findings.evidence: Both accessible_descriptions say 'secondary amine'; the first nugget's practice_check drills the opposite explicitly for the formula-identical sec-butylamine case.

location.anchor_text: a branched four-carbon amine, an amine flanked by two ethyl groups

findings.observation: The description states each distractor's nitrogen substitution outright but describes the key only as 'a branched four-carbon amine', saying nothing about how many carbons touch nitrogen. The key is the one option whose classification cannot be read off its description, so a learner can select it by elimination. The v2 twin does not have this asymmetry.
findings.learner_impact: The item stops measuring whether a screen-reader learner can apply the counting rule and starts measuring whether they notice which description is underspecified, on precisely the case the chapter most wants reasoned through.
findings.evidence: Options a=CC(C)(C)N, b=CCNCC, c=CN1CCCCC1, d=CCN(CC)CC with key a; find_accessibility_leaks returns clean because the asymmetry is semantic.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each option needs describing at the same level of structural detail so classification requires the same reasoning step from every learner.

location.anchor_text: silver oxide enters, yellow AgI precipitates and settles out

location.anchor_text: LiAlH4 delivers two hydride equivalents to the C#N triple bond

findings.evidence: Reader markdown contains 10^11, 10^6, C#N triple bond, Ar-N#N+; Unicode sub/superscript count across all 10 text blocks is zero.

location.anchor_text: Every comparison of amine basicity in this chapter

findings.evidence: Section text-block lengths 2637 to 4171 characters; markdown heading count zero in every block.

personas.summary: The figure set is technically clean: all 26 SMILES render correctly, no asset uses annotation_font_scale, and question option sets are illustrated all-or-nothing so there is no lone-illustrated-option answer tell. What the chapter lacks is visual load-bearing. All 26 figures are static single-molecule snapshots; none shows a relationship, sequence, orbital, resonance form, ordering, or comparison. The pKaH ladder, the pyrrole-vs-pyridine lone-pair geometry, aniline's resonance forms, and four of five multi-species mechanisms are carried entirely by prose. Layout compounds this: figures are appended after all section prose (415-667 words before the first figure), and the two densest numeric sections have the fewest figures. Two concrete defects: show_hydrogens is applied roughly inversely to teaching load, and it clutters pyrrole/imidazole in a way that camouflages the N-H versus bare-N distinction those figures exist to teach.

location.anchor_text: the nitrogen sits sp2-hybridized with its lone pair in the perpendicular p orbital

findings.observation: The pyrrole/pyridine distinction is entirely a statement about where a lone pair sits in space, rendered only as words. The three supporting assets are flat 2D structures physically incapable of showing orbital orientation; both rings look identical in the one respect that matters. The video brief scoped to carry it is deferred and compiles hidden with an empty url.
findings.learner_impact: This is the chapter's declared keystone; a student who cannot picture the two orbital orientations holds the distinction as a memorized verbal pair, producing wrong answers on basicity, EAS regiochemistry, SNAr and imidazole N1-vs-N3.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyrrole-imidazole and nugget-pyridine-chemistry orbital sentences; ch24-protonated-on-nitrogen-v2 option a; video-heterocycle-lone-pairs production_note claims the flat figures carry this content.
findings.recommended_outcome: Some representation distinguishing in-plane from perpendicular lone pairs for the two rings side by side is needed; the deferral note's claim that existing flat figures cover it is not accurate.

location.anchor_text: The numbers organize into families.

findings.observation: The pKaH ladder is stated as a running list of roughly eighteen values across two sections with no visual ordering anywhere. The section carries two figures marking only the top and bottom of the scale, and is the longest unbroken prose run in the chapter at 667 words.
findings.learner_impact: Ordering, spacing and family clustering are the entire content; the chapter then assesses exactly this relational skill in two rank_order items.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-basicity paragraphs 2-3; section figure count 2.
findings.recommended_outcome: A representation making the ordering and the two large discontinuities visible in one place is needed, spanning the alkylamine cluster and the delocalized outliers.

location.anchor_text: generating the key electrophile: an iminium ion

findings.observation: The section describes a four-species pathway and the reader shows only first and last. The carbinolamine and iminium ion are never drawn, though the entire NaBH3CN selectivity argument turns on the contrast between a neutral carbonyl and a positively charged C=N.
findings.learner_impact: The two figures present look like an unexplained jump from ketone to amine; a student asked to name the intermediate has never seen it depicted.
findings.evidence: nugget-reductive-amination iminium sentence; reader section 6 molecule blocks are only cyclohexanone and N-methylcyclohexylamine.
findings.recommended_outcome: Some depiction of the intermediate species, particularly the charged C=N against the neutral C=O, is needed.

location.anchor_text: the base must pull a hydrogen from the internal CH2

findings.observation: show_hydrogens is set roughly inversely to where hydrogens do teaching work. mol-sec-butylamine and mol-1-butene draw with every C-H explicit, flattening the skeleton into a straight stick; mol-tert-butylamine renders as a flat cross of eleven hydrogens obscuring the branching that is its entire point. Meanwhile mol-sec-butyltrimethylammonium, the one molecule whose beta hydrogens the argument is about, has no rdkit_options and is drawn with no hydrogens visible. The Hofmann section presents its three-stage sequence in two different notations.
findings.learner_impact: A student cannot track the same four-carbon skeleton across three panels drawn in different notations, and the regiochemical claim asks them to compare two sets of hydrogens on a structure where none are drawn.
findings.evidence: rdkit_options: mol-tert-butylamine, mol-butylamine, mol-sec-butylamine, mol-1-butene, mol-propanenitrile all show_hydrogens true; mol-sec-butyltrimethylammonium none.
findings.recommended_outcome: Explicit-hydrogen display should follow teaching load rather than molecule size, and notation should be consistent within a multi-panel sequence.

location.anchor_text: N3 has no hydrogen; its lone pair occupies an sp2 orbital in the ring plane

findings.observation: mol-pyrrole and mol-imidazole set show_hydrogens true, drawing all aromatic C-H bonds explicitly and surrounding the ring with hydrogens that compete with the one distinction the figure exists to teach. mol-histamine in the same section contains the same ring without the flag and renders a clean NH and a clean bare N.
findings.learner_impact: The section tells students to look at a drawn imidazole to find the nitrogen without a hydrogen, and the chapter's own drawn imidazole is the cluttered one; it also breaks the drawing convention used by every other aromatic asset.
findings.evidence: mol-pyrrole and mol-imidazole carry show_hydrogens true; mol-histamine carries none.
findings.recommended_outcome: The N-H versus bare-N contrast needs to be the most visually salient thing in those figures.

location.anchor_text: the regiochemistry is C2, and the reason is the standard EAS argument

findings.observation: The last three sections reason almost entirely in ring position numbers and not one heterocycle figure carries a position label. No asset uses an atom-numbering or annotation option; show_hydrogens is the only rdkit_option present anywhere.
findings.learner_impact: Students must map a numbering scheme onto figures that do not display it, and must already know the heterocycle numbering convention the chapter never states. This bites hardest on ch24-fused-heterocycle-reactivity, whose distractors name C2 and C3 of a bicycle it shows no structure of.
findings.evidence: nugget-pyrrole-imidazole and nugget-pyridine-chemistry position claims; all asset rdkit_options keys are show_hydrogens only.
findings.recommended_outcome: Position identity needs to be visible on the heterocycle figures and on the pyridine option structures.

location.anchor_text: Every comparison of amine basicity in this chapter

findings.observation: Every one of the ten compiled sections has the identical block order: all section prose in one text block, then all molecule blocks, then video, then links. No figure is adjacent to the sentence it supports. Word counts before the first figure: 415, 667, 631, 480, 532, 509, 564, 558, 613, 606. The two most number-dense sections carry the fewest figures.
findings.learner_impact: A figure arriving 600 words after its passage must be re-connected by the reader; a reader scanning figures first sees a gallery of unrelated molecules with no argument attached.
findings.evidence: Block-order dump of the compiled reader shows text-then-molecules-then-video-then-links in all ten sections with zero interleaving.
findings.recommended_outcome: Figure placement needs to be adjacent to the passage that uses it, and the basicity sections need more visual support than the concrete-structure sections, not less.

location.anchor_text: the replacement menu, which should be learned as a table because exams treat it as one

findings.evidence: nugget-arenediazonium-chemistry paragraph 3; reader section 8 shows only benzenediazonium, benzonitrile and the azo dye.
findings.recommended_outcome: The full menu needs to be readable at a glance, with the products it names actually depicted.

location.anchor_text: about 95% 1-butene

The one energy-profile item models a single pathway and does not depict the two competing transition states whose relative heights are the entire explanation.

findings.evidence: nugget-hofmann-elimination ratio sentence; reader section 7 molecule blocks; ch24-hofmann-profile control has three points and step_count 1.
findings.recommended_outcome: The alternative outcome and the reason it loses need to be visible alongside the winner.

location.anchor_text: the nitrogen also holds a lone pair, not drawn, at the fourth corner of its pyramid

findings.observation: All 26 assets carry an authored accessibility.long_description and all 10 nuggets carry a practice_check; the compiled reader contains zero occurrences of either. location.anchor_text: resonance structures can be drawn with a C=N double bond and a carbanion at the ortho or para position

The two figures show no charge separation and no comparison to the protonated form. The benzylamine/diphenylamine control comparison is delivered as three numbers in a sentence with neither compound depicted.

findings.evidence: nugget-arylamine-basicity resonance and conjugation-path sentences; reader section 3 shows only aniline and p-nitroaniline.

location.anchor_text: Piperidine (six-membered saturated ring, one N-H)

findings.observation: Structure support is applied unevenly by item rather than by need. Eleven option-bearing items supply structures for every option, but five intrinsically structural items supply none: ch24-rank-basicity, ch24-rank-aniline-substituents, ch24-classify-amine-classes, ch24-pyrrole-vs-pyridine and ch24-fused-heterocycle-reactivity. findings.recommended_outcome: Support needs to follow the demand of the task, and within a single option set the level of scaffolding needs to be uniform.

location.anchor_text: One hydrogen on atom 2

findings.learner_impact: Two of five labelled atoms cannot be pointed at, so the student holds an invisible beta hydrogen and an invisible counterion in memory while filling a five-row table.
findings.evidence: ch24-hofmann-e2-ledger student_config molecule_smiles CCC(C)[N+](C)(C)C with atom_labels id 3 and id 5; no rdkit_options field.

location.anchor_text: how many carbons does the product amine have, relative to what you started with?

findings.learner_impact: The section says exam problems turn on the difference between routes, and that difference is a four-way comparison the reader must assemble from four paragraphs; the isocyanate is the one genuinely unfamiliar structure and is never shown.
findings.evidence: nugget-amine-synthesis-reduction opening line and four route paragraphs; reader section 5 shows only propanenitrile and nitrobenzene.

executive_summary: Chapter 24 is chemically the cleanest package the pipeline has produced. The instructor persona verified all 26 asset SMILES and all 84 question structures with RDKit against formula, canonical connectivity and InChIKey, re-derived all 56 answer keys independently, and checked roughly twenty pKa values against literature: zero wrong structures, zero wrong keys, zero wrong values. The ch22 answer-leak class was avoided at baseline — both reaction-coordinate descriptions report curve geometry and relative heights without stating step count or thermodynamic classification, and the automated guard is clean across all 56 items. The baseline verdict is nevertheless BLOCKED, on three grounds. Two are chapter-local and were corrected the same day: both Hofmann drawing items described a primary amine as 'secondary' in the accessibility channel only — teaching, to non-visual learners exclusively, the exact misconception the chapter's first concept exists to destroy — and one numeric item handed the screen-reader learner the amine classification that is the whole of its answer. The third is the platform structure_scaffold input-path ticket (canvas-only drawing, no text entry), unresolved and identical to ch1/11/15-19/23, which forces 'blocked' on its own. Production's own coherence pass again introduced an error while closing a gap — the benzylamine/diphenylamine paragraph asserted that two aryl rings double the basicity discount, refuted by the two numbers printed beside it — repeating the ch23 pattern exactly. The chapter's real weakness is not chemistry but form: every one of its 26 figures is a static single molecule, so the pKaH ladder, the diazonium replacement menu, the pyrrole-versus-pyridine orbital geometry and four multi-step mechanisms are all carried by prose alone, and the chapter twice tells the reader that content 'should be learned as a table' without supplying one.
consensus_strengths: Zero chemistry errors and zero wrong answer keys across 56 items and 110 verified structures — the first chapter in this series to reach that on the baseline pass.

The reaction-coordinate accessible descriptions avoid the ch22 leak class entirely; both report plotted geometry and relative heights and neither names step count, rate-determining step, or thermodynamic direction.
Authoring-layer accessibility coverage is complete: 26 of 26 assets carry alt_text and long_description, 56 of 56 questions carry an accessible_description, and nothing is stubbed.
Thirteen of the fifteen question types are keyboard-operable as shipped, including rank_order Move up/down buttons that announce position and labelled selects on five other types.
The expanded prose is genuinely text-first: a learner who perceives no figure can still obtain every lone-pair geometry, every pKaH value, both regiochemical arguments and the 95:5 Hofmann ratio.

The two error_repair items are the strongest assessment design in the chapter — the flaw sits in the substrate, a correct-but-unflawed decoy is offered, and two repairs adjust conditions where no condition change can rescue a geometrically impossible step.
Option sets carry structures all-or-nothing, so the lone-illustrated-option answer tell found in ch15 and ch16 does not recur.
No asset sets annotation_font_scale; the oversized stereo-glyph defect of ch14/ch18 does not recur.
